notes:
Account snapshot: Silvercrest builds in-product assistants and contextual product search for mid-market B2B SaaS customers. They started on Hosted API to validate model outputs and UX; now evaluating Dedicated to get predictable throughput and lower per-token unit costs.

Key constraints and priorities (customer quotes and paraphrase):
- "We need <200ms median for chat snippeted into UI; some users tolerate 300ms but core product owners want <200ms."
- Data residency for EU customers is a must for certain large accounts.
- Cost sensitivity: primary metric is $/1k tokens + tail-latency impact on UX. Procurement pushing for fixed commitment vs pure usage billing.

POC / eval notes:
- Hosted API demo produced acceptable quality; sample prompts for product-help and doc search. Median latencies observed ~110-130ms for short-turn chat (20-60 tokens). Throughput in our sandbox was low (10-20 rps) — they want predictable 80-120 rps baseline.
- SE (Priya) recommended Dedicated reserved pool with autoscale + burst to meet spikes and keep average unit cost down. Suggested config: 2 x A100-equivalent per pool, KV prefix caching enabled for repeated product-context prompts, and batching policy tuned for 25-100ms added scheduling latency (expected token cost drop ~30-45%).
- Cost optimization workshop agenda (agreed): 1) token accounting and unit economics, 2) batching/cost vs latency trade-offs (live simulation on their trace), 3) prefix/KV caching setup and benchmarks, 4) quantization profiles recommendation for their LLM family, 5) routing/fallback policy to lower-cost variants during peak.

Action items from meeting:
- Redwood to run hosted->dedicated delta cost model for their 3-month projected usage and show break-even. (Deliverable: pricing model spreadsheet)
- Silvercrest infra to share 48h trace of production prompts (anonymized) for batching/caching sim. (Drive link sent)
- Schedule security deep-dive with infra security (SAML flow, KMS integration) — requested by 2024-12-12.

Stated objections / risks:
- Procurement: wants firm numbers for dedicated commit before signing.
- Infosec: needs ISO/SOC docs and a plan for EU residency.
- Engineering: conservative on quantization — want to validate no model-quality regressions on core intent detection tasks.

Quote from Product Lead (Ana M): "If we can cut our token spend by 30% while keeping latency under 220ms, this is a no-brainer. But we need numbers, not slides."
